title: Untrusted Internal RPCs (Missing Backend Authz)
pattern: Bypassing authorization validation checks in backend service methods under the assumption that the upstream proxy or frontend caller has already performed validation.
why_bad: Violates the security boundary principle of isolation. If an attacker compromises the frontend server, they can invoke arbitrary backend RPCs with spoofed parameters to modify or read any user's records.
detection: RPC service methods or endpoints receiving user identifiers as arguments without requiring cryptographically signed user token validation in the context of the call.
fix: Pass a cryptographically signed End-User Context (EUC) ticket from the frontend to the backend, enabling the backend to perform its own independent validation.
source: `Heather Adkins et al. - Building Secure and Reliable Systems (2020)`, Ch 6, p. 109-110.
